newsitem.title: JAPAN: "Commitment" too strong for Japan growth view - MOF.
newsitem.headline: "Commitment" too strong for Japan growth view - MOF.

text.p: It would be going too far to characterise Japan's policy of seeking domestic-led growth as a commitment or an assurance to the United States, Eisuke Sakakibara, a senior Finance Ministry official, told a news conference on Tuesday.

Asked whether Japan had any concrete measures with which to assure the United States of Japanese domestic demand-led growth, Sakakibara said: "First of all, I think words such as 'assurance' and 'commitment' are a bit strong. The situation is not like that."

Deputy U.S. Treasury Secretary Lawrence Summers had said earlier he welcomed what he called a commitment by Japan to take measures as needed to ensure a recovery led by strong domestic demand and to avoid a significant increase in its trade surplus.

"Minister of Finance Mitsuzuka made it clear that the Japanese government shared these objectives and he committed to take measures as necessary to ensure a strong demand-led recovery and avoid a significant increase in external imbalances," Summers had told a separate news conference.

Summers met Mitsuzuka earlier on Tuesday in Tokyo on the sidelines of a "Six Markets" meeting between finance and central bank officials of Japan, the United States, Australia, Hong Kong, Singapore and China.
Sakakibara said Mitsuzuka had explained to Summers that Japan's external demand was unlikely to grow significantly.
"The minister explained that Japan would like to achieve growth led by domestic demand," Sakakibara added.
